english_translation: My phone battery died, so I did not see your message.

dialogue.shona: Foni yangu yakadzima bhatiri saka handina kuona mashoko ako.
dialogue.english: My phone battery died, so I did not see your message.
dialogue.literal_gloss: Foni [foni] • yangu [yangu] • yakadzima [it (past) dzima] • bhatiri [bhatiri] • saka [so / therefore] • handina [I do not na] • kuona [to / at ona] • mashoko [plural shoko] • ako [ako]

grammar_notes.title: Talking About the Past ('yakadzima')
grammar_notes.content: The verb 'yakadzima' expresses a completed past action. Shona has two main ways to talk about the past: 1) For actions that happened earlier today or very recently, combine the short subject prefix ('nda-' = I, 'wa-' = you, 'a-' = he/she, 'ta-' = we, 'va-' = they) directly with the verb stem (e.g., 'ndamuka' = 'I woke up today', 'wabudirira' = 'you have succeeded'). 2) For events that happened yesterday or further in the past, insert '-ka-' after the subject prefix (e.g., 'takatenga' = 'we bought', 'vakaenda' = 'they went', 'akadanidzira' = 'he shouted').
grammar_notes.rule: Recent Today Past: [nda- / wa- / ta- / va-] + verb | Earlier Past: [ndaka- / waka- / taka- / vaka-] + verb

grammar_notes.title: Possessive Pronouns: Saying 'My', 'Your', and 'Our' ('yangu')
grammar_notes.content: In Shona, possessive words like 'yangu' ('my/your/our/their') always follow the noun they belong to! The six core possessive stems are '-ngu' (my), '-ko' (your), '-ke' (his/her/its), '-du' (our), '-nyu' (your plural/polite), and '-vo' (their). A short linking sound ('wa-', 'ya-', 'ra-', 'cha-', 'dza-', 'ma-') attaches to the front of the stem to match the noun: for example, 'shamwari yangu' (my friend), 'munda wako' (your field), 'mabhuku edu' (our books), and 'kubudirira kwenyu' (your success).

grammar_notes.title: Linking Ideas Smoothly with 'saka'
grammar_notes.content: Longer Shona sentences flow naturally by linking two clauses with connectors like 'saka'. The four essential connectors to master are: 'uye' ('and / furthermore' between two clauses), 'asi' ('but / however'), 'saka' ('so / therefore'), and 'nokuti' / 'nekuti' ('because').

cultural_notes.title: Mobile Phone Batteries ('Bhatiri reFoni') & Solar Charging
cultural_notes.content: When a mobile phone battery runs flat ('foni yakadzima bhatiri'), people politely explain why they missed messages ('mashoko'), and many households across urban and rural Zimbabwe use rooftop solar panels to keep phones and lights charged.

active_exercises.prompt: How do you politely ask someone to speak softly ('taura zvinyoronyoro')?
In 'Uya kuno undibatsire', what does the prefix '-ndi-' inside 'undibatsire' mean?
active_exercises.explanation: The object prefix '-ndi-' always means 'me', placed directly before the verb stem '-batsira' (help).

active_exercises.prompt: What does 'parutivi pemugwagwa' mean in 'Rori yakamira parutivi pemugwagwa'?

active_exercises.correct_answer: Beside the road / on the side of the road
active_exercises.explanation: 'Parutivi pe-' means 'beside / at the side of', and 'mugwagwa' is 'road'.
